text:
Columbus comes in on the second night of a back-to-back, fresh off a 2-1 shootout win over Dallas in which the Blue Jackets trailed in the third period and still won. Buffalo's three-game winning streak ended with a 2-1 home loss to Ottawa, and the Sabres are playing without Konsta Helenius, Justin Danforth and Matt Grzelcyk. Columbus won the October 1 meeting 6-3, a game it deserved to win 37% of the time (the share of simulated replays of every shot that it wins).

Neither side has been good at controlling chances. At five on five, the Blue Jackets have taken 49% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and the Sabres 50%. Buffalo's power play is slightly better, but it takes 4.1 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents chances. In net, projected starter Cam Talbot sits at +5.6 goals saved above expected this season, though he was at -13.7 last year. Projected Buffalo goalie Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is at -2.2 this season after a +9.1 year.

Tage Thompson is the player to watch: 42% to score and 74% for a point, with five goals in a four-game point streak. For Columbus, Zach Werenski is 68% for a point. Mathieu Olivier, never drafted, is one goal from 50 in the NHL. Our under-the-radar picks are both Sabres. Jason Zucker, a fourth-liner, has 2.3 expected goals in his last six games, and we have him at 23% to score. Jack Quinn is 65% for a point, above what his season pace says.
